lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Okay. I'm the merchant. You're the buyer. I have a wool blanket. I say it's worth fifteen copper. What do you say?

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: Is it worth fifteen copper?

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: That's not — you don't ask that. You say it's worth eight. Then I say twelve. Then you say ten. Then I sigh dramatically and say fine, eleven, and we both walk away feeling like we won.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: But if it's worth fifteen, why would I say eight?

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Because that's how haggling works.
lines.monologue: He's looking at me like I just explained that gravity goes sideways on Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Let's try again. I'm selling dried fish. I say twenty copper. Go.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: How long ago was it caught?

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: That's — okay, that's actually a good question, but you're supposed to—

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: Because if it was caught more than four days ago the salt content has to be higher to prevent spoilage, which means the actual nutritional value per copper is lower. So either it's fresh and worth twenty, or it's older and worth twelve based on what you're actually getting.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: I stare at him. He just deconstructed my asking price using food science. He's not haggling. He's doing quality assessment.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Fine. New item. A candle. I say five copper. It's a normal candle. There's nothing to analyze. Just tell me it's worth three.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: Five copper seems fair for a candle.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Caelan.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You're supposed to lie about what you think it's worth.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: Why would I lie to someone I'm trying to have a relationship with?
lines.monologue: He says it simply. Not philosophically. Like it's obvious. Like lying to a merchant is the same as lying to a friend and he can't tell the difference because to him there isn't one.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: This is infuriating. This is also the most honest conversation I've had in years and I don't know what to do with that.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You are the worst negotiator I've ever met.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: If you ever go to a market alone, you'll come back with no money and twelve things you overpaid for.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: Probably.
lines.monologue: He's smiling. Small. Like he knows he's bad at this and he's okay with that.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: I'm going to have to go to every market with him for the rest of our lives. This is a business expense. I'm categorizing it as loss prevention.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Same time tomorrow. We're going to work on your facial expressions. When someone names a price, you can't just accept it with your whole face.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I'll try.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You won't. But I appreciate the lie.
lines.monologue: Look at that. He's learning already.
